# 01 Parse minimal flowchart + timeline syntax into an AST, in a working workspace

## Outcome

`@siren/core` exists as a real pnpm package with TypeScript + Vitest wired up, and
`parseSiren(source: string)` turns Siren source text (a minimal `flowchart` header, node/edge
declarations, and a `timeline:` block) into a `SirenDocument` plus a diagnostics array, without
throwing on malformed input. Every cross-module type contract agreed in the spec is frozen in
`contracts.ts` so later tickets can build against it without waiting on this ticket's internals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm install && pnpm --filter @siren/core test` succeeds from a clean checkout.
- [ ] `parseSiren` on:
  ```
  flowchart TD
    A[Start]
    A --> B[Process]
    B --> C[End]

  timeline:
    step 1: enter B fade
    step 2: enter C fade
  ```
  returns a `SirenDocument` with 3 nodes (`A`, `B`, `C` — `B` and `C` declared inline on edges),
  2 edges, direction `TD`, and a timeline with steps `1` and `2`; `diagnostics` is empty.
- [ ] `parseSiren` also accepts `flowchart LR` and sets `direction: 'LR'`.
- [ ] `parseSiren` on a source with a malformed edge line (e.g. `A --> ` with no target) returns
  `document: null` (or best-effort partial) and at least one error-severity diagnostic; it does
  not throw.
- [ ] A node declared twice with different bracket text (`A[Start]` ... later `A[Begin]`) parses
  successfully and produces a warning diagnostic; the first label wins.
- [ ] `packages/core/src/contracts.ts` exports `SirenDocument`, `Diagnostic`, `GraphModel`,
  `ResolvedTimeline`, `PositionedGraph`, `TextMeasurer`, `AnimationController`, and
  `SirenRenderResult`, matching the shapes agreed in the spec's Design Contract section.

## Test seam

`parseSiren(source: string): { document: SirenDocument | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }` —
unit level, pure function, no DOM/environment dependency.
